name: code_read_file
description:
Read one file of Ledgerline's codebase by its exact path, relative to the repository root, as code_search prints it (src/api/uploads.ts). Use it after a search has named a likely file, to confirm that file holds the code the issue is about. Paths are case-sensitive: src/Report.ts and src/report.ts are different files. The config/ directory cannot be read. It costs one local read and no money, but a long file costs many tokens, so read the file a search pointed to rather than browsing.

Returns JSON: {"path": ..., "total_lines": n, "total_chars": n, "shown_chars": n, "truncated": false, "content": <the file's text>}. A response is capped: concise returns at most the first 6,000 characters, detailed at most the first 20,000; a longer file comes back cut at the cap with "truncated": true. An empty file is a success with "content": "" and total_lines 0: the file exists and has nothing in it. A path that does not exist is an error that names the closest existing paths.

path.description: The file's path relative to the repository root, exactly as a search result printed it, with the same capital letters: src/util/retry.ts, not /src/util/retry.ts, ./src/util/retry.ts or retry.ts. A directory is not a file.

response_format.description: concise, the cheap default, returns the first 6,000 characters, which holds most of this codebase's files whole. detailed returns up to 20,000 characters and costs up to three times as much; choose it only when a concise read came back "truncated": true and the code you need is past the cut.

examples.note: The typical call: a path exactly as code_search printed it, concise.

A hard case: three files differ only by case or extension (src/Report.ts, src/report.tsx, src/reports.ts); keep the capital letters the search printed, and ask for detailed only because a concise read came back truncated.
